name: Help Scout
reason: Help Scout now also operates a hosted MCP endpoint (https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp), generally available; per the batch's own convention (Podio/Pylon/Slack drafts list mcp when an official server exists) the protocols list should include mcp.

name: Help Scout
reason: The draft's 'none_found' for a vendor MCP is wrong: Help Scout's own blog announced its MCP server is out of beta and generally available, hosted at https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp (read-only, per-user OAuth, Standard/Plus/Pro plans). The draft missed it because it is documented in the help center (docs.helpscout.com), not the developer portal it searched. Composio HELP_SCOUT toolkit (129 tools, OAuth2) and the drewburchfield community server both re-confirmed.

name: fanbasis
reason: The very docs site the draft cited as MCP evidence now has an 'AI Agent / Connect an AI Agent' section documenting the official Commas MCP Connector: a one-click Claude Desktop MCP extension (available now, authenticated with the seller's API key), 11+ read tools plus confirmation-gated write actions (charge, refund, discount management, subscription changes), and a planned remote endpoint at https://www.fanbasis.com/mcp for ChatGPT/Grok. There is also a vendor-authored commas-cli npm package (author otniel@fanbasis.com) that fronts a hosted Commas MCP server. The draft's none_found is wrong or stale. The absence of a Composio toolkit (composio.dev/toolkits/fanbasis 404) still holds.

name: Clay
reason: Since the draft, Clay launched a documented Public API with an OpenAPI spec (developers.clay.com/openapi.json): people/company Searches (structured filters + advanced query language), Routines execution (Clay-managed functions, custom functions, Workflows alpha) including async runs and JSONL batch runs with presigned uploads, Tables structured query (Enterprise), outbound webhooks for run completion, pagination, rate limits and error contracts, plus a CLI and agent plugin. That is materially broader than 'narrow' (which was premised on 'no public versioned REST API or OpenAPI spec' — no longer true).

name: Clay
reason: The premise ('general table CRUD / workflow control via a public API does not exist') is stale. The Public API now offers self-serve API keys, searches, routine/function execution, batch runs, table queries (Enterprise), completion webhooks and an OpenAPI spec — an integration can be built today against documented endpoints.

name: Clay
reason: With the Public API launched, the API is no longer the blocker. Remaining caveats are quota/plan-shaped, not access-shaped: free-plan search quota is tiny (100 results/month), the Tables API is Enterprise-only, and credit consumption applies — but a self-serve integration is unblocked, consistent with buildable_now.

name: Brex
reason: Brex now also operates an official hosted MCP endpoint at https://api.brex.com/mcp (HTTP transport, OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration or Brex API token), so the protocol list should include mcp alongside rest.

name: Brex
reason: The draft states 'No official Brex vendor MCP server found on developer.brex.com', but Brex publishes one: developer.brex.com/docs/mcp documents the official Brex MCP server hosted at https://api.brex.com/mcp (beta; enabled via Settings > Beta features 'Brex in AI assistants' after an admin accepts the developer API agreement; OAuth via accounts-api.brex.com with RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration, or admin API token; ~44 tools spanning expenses, users, cards, banking, bills, vendors, accounting, travel, including write actions like update_expense_memo and receipt upload). Brex also announced it at brex.com/journal/brex-mcp-connect-brex-to-ai-tools. The Composio BREX toolkit (84 tools) is separately confirmed at composio.dev/toolkits/brex, so that half of the draft value stands.

name: Grain
reason: Grain also operates an official hosted MCP server at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp, documented in the same vendor developer docs the draft cited (developers.grain.com/mcp, 'Official Grain MCP Server: Quick Start Guide') and announced in Grain's June 18, 2025 release note. Protocols should include mcp alongside rest.

name: Grain
reason: An official vendor MCP server exists and is easy to find in vendor docs: developers.grain.com/mcp documents the 'Official Grain MCP Server' at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp (OAuth, tools like list_meetings/fetch_meeting_transcript/fetch_meeting_notes, usable in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor via mcp-remote), with a matching support article (support.grain.com/en/articles/14811968-grain-mcp) and the June 2025 release note calling it 'Grain's official MCP server... available now for all users'. The draft's claim that no MCP appears in developers.grain.com is wrong. The Composio part of the draft's mcp_notes does hold: docs.composio.dev/toolkits/grain.md still returns 404.
